appearance.description: 2026-08-19 (identity vs appearance split): generic, non-identifying physical characteristics ONLY - shape, material, generic colour language, texture (e.g. 'a cylindrical glass bottle, matte label, warm amber liquid') - MUST NEVER contain a brand name, product name, or any other identity-revealing text. `description` (above) still carries full identifying detail as before, unchanged - this is a SEPARATE, additive field, not a replacement. Meaningful mainly for kind 'product' or 'logo'/'prop' objects that carry a brand mark: identity (name, specific label wording) must never transfer into a Besque draft, but generic appearance facts (silhouette, material, colour) may safely inform composition. null/omitted (a pre-existing blueprint predating this field, or an object the model didn't classify) falls back to `description` wherever appearance would otherwise be quoted - additive and optional, never required, so a pre-existing blueprint remains valid unchanged.

brand.description: 2026-08-19 (per-object brand identity): the specific brand/company name this object visibly belongs to or names - the advertiser's own brand, OR a third-party brand appearing in the frame (e.g. a comparison ad showing a rival's product). A single, clean value distinct from `description` (which may also carry the name as part of ordinary prose) and from `appearance` (which must NEVER carry a brand/product name - see that field's own docstring). Exists so anything downstream that needs to know WHICH brand an object belongs to can read one structured value instead of parsing free text. null/omit when ownership is 'generic'/'besque'/'person', or when no specific brand name is actually legible/attributable in the image - never guess a brand from generic visual cues alone. Purely descriptive: it does NOT drive disposition (ownership/carries_brand_mark already do that, unchanged) and must never be quoted into any image-generation prompt text - the same identity-must-never-transfer principle `appearance` exists to enforce. Additive and optional - a pre-existing blueprint predating this field remains valid and unaffected.

required_in_output.description: 2026-08-19: presence in the reference is evidence this object exists in the SOURCE photo, not an instruction to reproduce it in the output - this field states which one applies. false = this was observed in the reference but is NOT structurally required to survive into the Besque draft (e.g. a stray hand mid-gesture, a loose hair strand, incidental background clutter that isn't load-bearing to the ad's own composition or argument) - only ever meaningful for disposition=='keep' objects, and NEVER overrides disposition=='substitute'/'drop', which already have their own explicit handling. true (or null/omitted) = required, the ordinary case - reproduce/substitute as disposition already says. This field is NEVER honoured for kind=='product' objects regardless of its stored value - the Besque product is always required in the output; see generate_image_prompt._objects_clause's own explicit guard for why this is enforced structurally, not left to this field alone. null/omitted (a pre-existing blueprint predating this field) is treated as true - every existing KEEP instruction renders byte-identical to before this field existed. Additive and optional, never required.

serves_object_id.description: 2026-08-17 (Problem 1 restoration): the object_id of the object THIS object exists to support - e.g. a hand holding the competitor's product records the product's object_id here. Meaningful for kind 'text' or 'prop' only (a caption pointing at a product, a hand/prop holding or staging one); null when this object stands on its own, which is the common case. Additive and optional - never required, so a pre-existing blueprint with no relational data on any object remains valid unchanged.

same_product_as.description: 2026-08-18 (three-voices product-count fix): the object_id of an EARLIER product object in this SAME list that this object is the SAME product as, differing only in size or format (e.g. a standard-size and a jumbo-size bottle of one product line). Meaningful for kind 'product' only. null (or omit) when this product is visually distinct from every other product object in the scene, which is the common single-product case, OR when this IS the earliest instance of a repeated product (it never names itself). Two-or-more product objects sharing a same_product_as chain are treated as multiple INSTANCES of the one authorised Besque bottle (all substitute, matching the reference's own count/layout); product objects that name no same_product_as and are not named BY one are each a DISTINCT product, of which only one substitutes and the rest drop - see deconstruct.resolve_product_group_dispositions. THIS IS NEVER THE RIGHT FIELD for a component, attachment, detached piece, container, or accessory of another object (a lid, cap, box, carton, dropper, applicator, spoon, refill pouch, sleeve) - see part_of below for that relationship instead; same_product_as means a separate, free-standing instance of the identical product, never a piece of one. Additive and optional - a pre-existing blueprint with no relational data on any object remains valid unchanged and is treated as every product object being distinct, the same behaviour as before this field existed.

part_of.description: 2026-08-20 (tin+lid product-count fix): the object_id of an EARLIER object in this SAME list that THIS object is a physical component, attachment, detached piece, container, or accessory OF - a lid, cap, box, carton, dropper, applicator, spoon, refill pouch, or sleeve belonging to a product object elsewhere in this list. Meaningful for any kind, most commonly 'product' or 'prop'. This is NOT the same relationship as same_product_as (above): same_product_as means a SEPARATE, free-standing instance of the identical product (a second bottle of the same line, a different size/format); part_of means this object is not a free-standing item at all, it has no independent existence in the composition apart from the object it belongs to. Getting this right matters - a detached lid or cap wrongly recorded as same_product_as is treated as a second full product instance and gets its own Besque bottle substituted in; the correct field for it is part_of, which never increments the authorised product count and always resolves to 'drop' once its parent is substituted (see deconstruct.resolve_disposition and generate_image_prompt.resolve_authorised_product_count). null (or omit) when this object is not a component of anything else, which is the common case. Never name yourself, and only ever name an object_id you have already assigned earlier in this SAME list. Additive and optional - a pre-existing blueprint with no relational data on any object remains valid unchanged.

social_proof_kind.description: 2026-08-19 (duplicate-testimonial guard + aggregate-vs-quote restoration): restores structural_zones[].social_proof_kind's aggregate_bar vs single_quote distinction, deleted by 6b82f60 with no replacement. Meaningful only when text_purpose is 'testimonial'. 'single_quote' = one customer's own words; 'aggregate' = a review-count/star-average summary with no single customer's words (e.g. 'Rated 4.8 by 12,000 customers') - Besque has no approved aggregate figure, so an aggregate-shaped object is ALWAYS dropped, never substituted, regardless of context - see deconstruct.resolve_testimonial_dispositions. null/omitted (a pre-existing blueprint predating this field, or a testimonial object the model didn't classify) is treated as 'single_quote' - the common case, and the same behaviour every testimonial-purposed object had before this field existed. Additive and optional, never required - a pre-existing blueprint remains valid unchanged.

typography.description: 2026-08-17 (per-zone typography restoration): restores the deleted top-level typography_zones array's per-zone typographic TREATMENT, deleted by 6b82f60 with no replacement - recorded per-object here instead of a separate position-matched array, since text objects already carry a stable object_id/bbox. Meaningful only for kind 'text'. Content substitution (which words land here, whether this object survives at all) is governed elsewhere (disposition/text_purpose) - this states HOW an object that DOES survive is dressed, so a reference with several distinct typographic levels (a large serif headline, a gold small-caps accent line, small sans body copy, a CTA button label) doesn't collapse into one style by default. null/omitted (a pre-existing blueprint predating this field, or a text object the model didn't classify) produces no typographic instruction for that object, same as every text object had before this field existed - additive and optional, never required.

styling.description: 2026-08-17 (testimonial styling restoration): restores the deleted testimonial_zones[].styling field (card style, star-rating presence, quote-mark treatment - e.g. 'quote marks, no card', '5-star rating above the quote inside a white rounded card'), deleted by 6b82f60 with no replacement. Meaningful only when text_purpose is 'testimonial'. Content (the actual quote/attribution rendered) NEVER comes from this field - it always comes from the real, separately-selected customer review (select_testimonial_review); this field governs the CONTAINER's presentation only. null/omitted (a pre-existing blueprint predating this field, or a testimonial object the model didn't classify) produces a generic container instruction, the same behaviour every testimonial-purposed object had before this field existed - additive and optional, never required.

text_content.description: 2026-08-20 (text sub-objects, DETECTION ONLY): legible text baked into THIS object's own rendered pixels - a brand wordmark printed on a product's label, a logo on packaging, a caption burned into a background graphic - regardless of the parent object's own `kind`. This is the fix for a live, confirmed leak: competitor copy baked into a non-text object (a product label, a gradient-panel graphic) never became its own kind=='text' object, so resolve_disposition was never consulted on it at all and it rendered unchanged into Besque drafts twice - 'Norse Organics' on a gradient panel, 'KilgourMD' on both bottle labels. Every entry here goes through the EXACT SAME resolve_disposition machinery as a top-level kind=='text' object (same text_purpose enum, same ownership/carries_brand_mark-drives-disposition rule) - a sub-object with carries_brand_mark true or ownership 'competitor_branded' can never resolve to 'keep', identical to the top-level enforcement. `content` (the literal on-image string) is ANALYSIS-ONLY: it exists so a human/mechanical check can see what text was actually detected and confirm disposition was judged correctly, but it must NEVER be emitted into a built image-generation prompt - see generate_image_prompt.build_image_prompt's own end-of-build assertion, which raises if any text_content[].content string appears verbatim in the assembled prompt. A parent object with no legible baked-in text omits this field entirely (or an empty array) - the common case, unaffected. Additive and optional - a pre-existing blueprint predating this field remains valid unchanged. DETECTION ONLY: no message-level or claim analysis of what the text SAYS is performed here or anywhere downstream of it - only whether it exists, who it belongs to, and whether it may survive.

owner.description: 2026-08-19 (B1, schema/prompt contradiction fix): deconstruct.py's BLUEPRINT_PROMPT ('owner is the brand/body the proof belongs to, or null') has always told the model null is a legitimate value here - the plain 'string' type below never allowed it, causing a live, non-deterministic schema-validation failure ('None is not of type string') with no other change to the input. offer.type/value/mechanic were audited for the same contradiction and are NOT changed - the prompt documents only the whole `offer` object as nullable ('or null if no offer'), never these three sub-fields individually, so loosening them would not be matching a documented contract, just guessing.
